item.text: {"question_id":"2B.8","answer":"In 2023, Tshisekedi attributed military reform, mobilization, and capacity-building to ongoing insecurity involving M23 and ADF, civilian protection, and national defense, and issued or publicly endorsed related measures including army support, regional operations, and an Armed Defence Reserve for Wazalendo fighters (BATCH-0006-E001; BATCH-0010-E008; BATCH-0019-E010; BATCH-0022-E003). The state also had formal budget, internal-control, audit, prior-review, treasury-planning, and public-disclosure requirements, and the 2023 accounts were later subject to parliamentary review (BATCH-0017-E005; BATCH-0029-E005; BATCH-0024-E002). These frameworks and aggregate execution figures show governance structures and some contrary evidence to an exclusively opaque-resource account, but do not establish conflict-specific transparency, procurement compliance, proportionality, or effective operation of safeguards (BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0029-E005). The adverse record is that the administration pursued a strongly militarized approach, supported irregular forces, contracted private military personnel, acquired armed drones, and faced continuing violence and displacement, raising concerns about escalation and effectiveness (BATCH-0011-E019; BATCH-0028-E016; BATCH-0012-R07-E003; BATCH-0010-E003). The supplied evidence does not prove that these measures enriched networks or were intended to intimidate neighbors; nor does it isolate Tshisekedi’s responsibility for the adverse outcomes from armed groups, Rwanda, regional forces, and inherited institutional weakness. Overall, the record supports genuine security pressures and formal resource-governance mechanisms, but remains materially insufficient to conclude that military budgets, mobilization, and procurement were consistently transparent and proportionate.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E001","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0019-E010","BATCH-0022-E003","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0022-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E019","BATCH-0028-E016","BATCH-0012-R07-E003","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0024-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence provides defense-budget line items, procurement audits, contract beneficiaries, conflict-specific execution data, or reliable proportionality comparisons with the identified threats.","Formal controls and later aggregate budget execution do not establish compliance, implementation, or independence of oversight in military spending.","The supplied evidence does not prove enrichment of networks or intimidation of neighbors.","Security outcomes and displacement have multiple causes, including armed groups, Rwanda, regional forces, and inherited institutional weakness; the evidence does not isolate presidential causation.","Some adverse evidence covers the broader presidency or conditions preceding 2023 rather than a separately measured 2023 military-resource record."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that private contracting, armed-drone acquisition, or irregular-force support proved network enrichment or intimidation.","Recast general budget frameworks and presidential directives as formal governance context and stated policy, not proof of transparent or proportionate defense spending.","Added the omitted contrary evidence on spending-priority directives, budget execution, parliamentary review, and formal audit and disclosure controls.","Preserved the documented security rationale while separating it from evidence of implementation, proportionality, procurement transparency, and outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if defense-budget allocations, procurement records, audits, contracting beneficiaries, or evidence of operational compliance become available.","Reopen if independent evidence clarifies whether the Armed Defence Reserve, Wazalendo support, private military contracting, or armed-drone procurement were proportionate and lawfully controlled.","Reopen if evidence establishes ruler-specific responsibility for military-resource abuses or demonstrates effective corrective oversight during 2023."]}
